(3) Dimension names/weights: scoring.toml gates render/constraints and weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2, floor 0.05 - none of those words or numbers is stated as grading machinery in the brief; the brief's 'Board, Conversations and Activity views' (instruction.md:11) are product views, not dimensions. (4) Test paths: the brief names only /app, /app/server.js, /app/app.db, /assets/seed_data.json, /instructions/hireops_rules.md, /instructions/integration.md, GET /api/health (instruction.md:11-15); no /tests, /logs/verifier, score.py or restart_mcp.py. environment/Dockerfile:14-15 copies only instructions/ and assets/. (5) Sentinels/probes: judge prompts use per-review suffixed names and generic letters (J1, A-F, V-Z) plus the literal 'plain' (functional prompt.md protocol T); none appears in the brief/notes. Seeded values the judge reads (Greta Lindqvist, the Noor note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.') come from seed data, not judge-created probes, and are not named in the brief. Demo accounts/password in instruction.md:17 are the profile-expected credentials (SKILL.md known false positive), not grader machinery. (6) Verbatim overlap: no 10-word shingle shared between brief+notes and any criterion description or judge prompt; at 7 words only 4 shared shingles across all 56 criteria, each a criterion restating a public rule fragment ('its most recent 30 messages oldest of', 'the reason is shown and keyboard focus', 'to the stage it was rejected from') - criteria quoting the spec, not the brief quoting the rubric. (7) The brief is task-authored, not the template placeholder (template instruction.md:1 'CHANGE_ME...' absent). Counterexample attempts: a weak app cannot game anything from the brief because it exposes no criterion list, probe value, weight or test path; a conforming app cannot be penalised by this row since nothing in the brief binds it to grader vocabulary. Scope note: this is a source review of the agent-visible prompt and notes; check-instruction-hygiene.py itself was not executed (deterministic reviewer's row), and no runtime evidence is needed for this row.
